title: Garden Schools
program: Pre-K, elementary and middle schools, library, recreation center, community hub
summary: Three schools and a recreation center on one Philadelphia block, set in a landscape the whole neighborhood can use.
body: What makes a school look like a school? Usually four things: it reads as an institution, it makes one featured architectural move, it contrasts with everything around it, and above all it looks secure. The question this project starts from is what might come after that.

The answer borrowed here is the garden cemetery. Before America had public parks, the garden cemetery was its first designed public landscape — people walked, picnicked and spent afternoons in them. A garden school works the same way: the grounds are the neighborhood's garden, and the school sits inside it rather than behind a fence.

One Philadelphia block holds a Pre-K and kindergarten, an elementary school, and a middle school combined with a library and recreation center, with parking tucked underneath and a community hub at the eastern end. Between and around them the landscape stays open — wetlands and a boardwalk, a learning canopy, a theater, pool, fields and courts — so the block is in use long after the school day ends.

How the block is organised: Pre-K and kindergarten to the west, elementary south, middle east, with the community hub and indoor recreation, parking beneath, and the drop-offs kept apart.
